data.description:

The company and its shareholders are offering 50M shares at an indicated price range of $40 to $44, for a total deal size of $2B to $2.2B. Accelevation (ACCV) is also expected to start trading during the week.

Tuesday - September 29

  • All day - The three-day NetApp (NTAP) Insight Conference will begin. The event focused on data infrastructure, cloud strategy, AI, and cyber resilience will include participation by Nvidia (NVDA) executives.
  • All day - The CEO outlook session at the Global Gaming Expo will feature MGM Resorts (MGM) CEO Bill Hornbuckle, Caesars Entertainment (CZR) CEO Tom Reeg, and Wynn Resorts (WYNN) CEO Craig Billings.

 

Wednesday - September 30

  • Earnings watch - Notable companies due to report include Micron Technology (MU), Jabil (JBL), and Conagra Brands (CAG).
  • Fedspeak - Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, and Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari are all scheduled to speak at separate events.

For every Corteva share held at the close of the September 24 record date, a shareholder is due one Vylor share. data.title: Genentech's Gazyva gains indication for idiopathic nephrotic syndrome
data.description:
• The US FDA approved Roche (RHHBY)-owned Genentech's Gazyva (obinutuzumab) for an additional indication, idiopathic nephrotic syndrome.
  • The condition is characterized by large amounts of protein leaking into urine from the kidneys, leading to edema around the eyes, abdomen, feet, and legs.
  • Approval, for those two years and older, was based on the results of the phase 3 INShore trial in which more of those treated with Gazyva achieved sustained complete remission at week 52 compared to those on CellCept (mycophenolate mofetil).
  • Gazyva is already approved for lupus nephritis and several leukemia and lymphoma indications.

data.title: 3M upgraded at Bernstein on R&D structural change, less PFAS risk than expected
data.description:
3M (MMM) gained 1.4% in Friday's trading as Bernstein upgraded shares to Market Perform from Underperform with a $171 price target, raised from $145, reflecting a "refreshed understanding" of the company's transformation following a recent meeting with management.

Bernstein analyst Varun Govindaraj said he now believes 3M (MMM) has been structurally transformed through an "R&D factory" approach that manages product commercialization like a portfolio, with pipeline reviews, data, and an ROI focus for capital deployment.

Previous issues that affected R&D effectiveness—PFAS replacement, fewer but bigger bets, healthcare draining capital—no longer impact the organization going forward, the analyst said, largely driving his improved organic growth forecast for 3M (MMM) to 3.5%-4% from ~3% in his discounted cash flow model.

Govindaraj said 3M (MMM) is in the early stages of a short-cycle recovery, likely driven by AI capex, that should last for another couple of years, and as "the quintessential short-cycle business, 3M has a secular tailwind from this."

The analyst thinks PFAS is less of a risk than previously thought, seeing 3M (MMM) as well-positioned to absorb any incremental negative news; the company is in negotiations with plaintiffs on personal injury lawsuits rather than going through a bellwether case process, which is a "positive sign" and could largely eliminate previous concerns over a multi-year overhang.

Govindaraj said he is "comfortable" with 3M's (MMM) ability to reach ~25% operating margins in 2026 with gross margins gradually rising to the mid-40s and possibly higher over the back half of this decade.

data.title: Ligand Pharma a new Outperform at Barclays on biopharma royalty aggregation
data.description:
• Barclays initiated Ligand Pharmaceuticals (LGND) with an Outperform rating, saying that the company's transition to loyalty aggregation has the potential to generate long-term revenue growth of greater than 20%.
  • The investment bank has a price target of $345 (~15% upside based on Sept. 24 close). 
  • Analyst Glan Santangelo said that despite Ligand's strong performance year-to-date—up ~59%—"core fundamentals and outlook remain somewhat underappreciated especially given the expanded deal team + ample cash generation, which increases the company's ability to source and execute deals."
  • He added that the company has flexibility to execute its business strategy given it has ~$700M in cash and projected free cash flow of ~$300M in 2027.
  • Santagelo noted that Ligand has seven near-term pipeline catalysts with estimated peak royalties of more than $600M.

data.title: Evonik gains after report of BASF takeover approach (update)
data.description:
Update 2:18pm: Adds BASF comment.

Evonik (EVKIY) (EVKIF) rose 7.2% in German trading after a report that BASF (BASFY) (BFFAF) approached its German chemical rival about a takeover. BASF fell 3.6%.

BASF (BASFY) recently made a proposal to Evonik (EKVIY) and its largest holders, the RAG-Stiftung foundation, according to a Financial Times report  on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter.

Evonik (EVKIF) confirmed in a statement on Friday that it received a non-binding approach from BASF (BASFY) on a takeover offer for all of Evonik's shares. No talks are currently taking place. Evonik declined to comment beyond its legal obligations.

BASF said in a separate statement that it has had exploratory talks with RAG-Stiftung and Evonik about a potential takeover. The "course and outcome" of the talks "remain open" at this stage.

BASF (BASFY) has been talking to advisers about a potential offer for Evonik (EVKIY) since earlier this year and is continuing to work on a possible deal, according to the FT report. The position of RAG-Stiftung, which has a 44% stake in Evonik, will be key to whether any transaction can happen.

RAG-Stiftung declined to comment to the FT. 

The FT item comes after Dealreporter on Monday first reported that BASF (BASFY) explored a potential deal with Evonik (EVKIF) this year.  One source downplayed the possibility of a deal as BASF is "cash constrained" and will get the Agricultural Solutions IPO completed before it does an acquisition.

data.title: Beyond GLP-1 injectables, who wins the next phase for obesity drugs?
data.description:
Investors Should Know: The obesity drug market is undergoing a structural shift, moving beyond the initial injectable GLP-1 franchise. Now, the industry is moving toward a broader competitive landscape defined by oral agents, less-frequent dosing, multi-mechanism combinations, and entirely new biological targets. As more products reach late-stage development, companies will increasingly compete on tolerability, adherence, dosing convenience, and manufacturing economics rather than peak weight-loss efficacy alone.

Key Takeaways

  • Oral small-molecule GLP-1 therapies appear to be expanding the eligible patient pool rather than simply replacing injectables, drawing in patients new to this class of treatment.
  • Monthly dosing regimens are shifting the competitive conversation from initial weight loss toward long-term adherence and maintenance, a dimension that could reshape how payers and physicians evaluate products.
  • Multi-mechanism approaches, including GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonists and GLP-1/amylin combinations, represent the clearest attempt to compete on metabolic breadth rather than convenience alone.
  • Non-incretin mechanisms, targeting pathways outside the GLP-1 system, could expand treatment choice for patients who respond poorly to or cannot tolerate current agents, and may eventually pressure pricing across the broader class.
  • Analyst sentiment on smaller names is sharply divided: the same companies attracting strong-conviction bullish calls are also drawing bearish arguments centered on commoditization risk and replication by larger competitors.

Background: How the Obesity Drug Market Is Moving Beyond GLP-1 Injectables

The first generation of obesity drugs to achieve broad commercial scale were injectable GLP-1 and GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists. These products demonstrated meaningful weight loss in large trials and created a new treatment category. The current phase of development is layering additional dimensions on top of that foundation.

As the market develops, multiple sources of differentiation are emerging. There are oral small-molecule therapies that improve convenience and manufacturing scalability. At the same time, companies are working on less-frequent dosing formats including monthly maintenance regimens, as well as multi-mechanism agents that combine GLP-1 with GIP, amylin, or glucagon targets. In addition, there are non-incretin approaches that may address tolerability, lean mass preservation, or metabolic comorbidities.

The commercial implication is that weight-loss efficacy alone may become insufficient to sustain premium pricing as the field broadens.

Stocks to Watch: LLY, NVO, RHHBY, VKTX, GPCR, KTRA

Eli Lilly (LLY) and Novo Nordisk (NVO) are the two established commercial leaders in the obesity drug space, each with approved injectable and oral products and active late-stage pipelines. Roche (RHHBY) is building a diversified metabolic pipeline that spans incretin, amylin, oral, and muscle-related programs.

Among smaller biotechnology companies, Viking Therapeutics (VKTX) is advancing both oral and injectable versions of VK2735 alongside a monthly maintenance program, while Structure Therapeutics (GPCR) is pairing a late-stage oral GLP-1 candidate with a separate oral amylin program. Kailera Therapeutics (KTRA) is a clinical-stage company with an oral obesity candidate and a late-stage pipeline, though its commercial differentiation remains a subject of active analyst debate.

News Roundup

  • Eli Lilly's CEO discussed international Foundayo expansion and manufacturing investment, noting the oral obesity pill had captured approximately one-third of new oral obesity-pill prescriptions and that small-molecule production economics support international scale.
  • Viking Therapeutics announced positive topline results from a maintenance-dosing study of VK2735, with patients transitioning from weekly induction to less-frequent regimens retaining a substantial portion of initial weight loss and no material worsening of gastrointestinal adverse events.
  • Viking's maintenance data also included evaluation of oral maintenance regimens, creating a potential treatment architecture spanning injectable induction, less-frequent maintenance, and an oral option.
  • Roche reported that its once-weekly GLP-1/GIP agonist enicepatide reached both primary endpoints in a mid-stage trial, with a separate announcement confirming positive Phase 2 results in adults with type 2 diabetes and overweight or obesity.
  • Novo Nordisk reported Phase 3 CagriSema results showing favorable outcomes against a lower dose of Lilly's Zepbound in one trial and meaningful weight loss against placebo in another, though the comparator did not use the highest available Zepbound dose.
  • Novo also outlined 2030 ambitions including expanded oral GLP-1 capacity and multiple multi-blockbuster launch targets, alongside plans to diversify into adjacent therapeutic areas as competition in obesity intensifies.

What Analysts Say

SA contributor coverage of the obesity drug space reflects strong conviction in several directions, but also significant disagreement, particularly around smaller biotechnology names. Bullish analysts emphasize platform differentiation, pipeline breadth, and dosing optionality. Bearish arguments center on commoditization risk and the ability of larger companies to replicate what smaller developers are building.

The sharpest disagreement in recent coverage concerns Viking Therapeutics, where two analysts reached opposite conclusions from the same maintenance data. Roche and Structure Therapeutics attracted more uniformly positive assessments, while Kailera drew a split verdict.

Analyst Commentary

Stephen Ayers: Structure Therapeutics (GPCR) — Ayers holds a Strong Buy view on Structure, citing the company's combination of a late-stage oral GLP-1 candidate and a separate oral amylin program as a platform strategy that reduces development risk and is harder for competitors to replicate than a single oral agent. Favorable 72-week data, low discontinuation rates, and the absence of drug-induced liver injury are identified as key supporting factors. Read more about Structure's pipeline.

Terry Chrisomalis: Viking Therapeutics (VKTX) — Chrisomalis rates Viking Strong Buy, emphasizing that positive maintenance-study results for VK2735 and the company's combination of oral, injectable, and monthly-dosing options create a differentiated treatment architecture that spans multiple patient preferences and stages of care. Read more on Viking's optionality.

Stephen Ayers: Viking Therapeutics (VKTX) — Taking the opposing view, Ayers rates Viking Sell, arguing that monthly dosing convenience and autoinjector features are replicable by larger competitors with greater manufacturing and commercial resources. He contends the market for undifferentiated obesity drugs could become commoditized, limiting Viking's long-term pricing power. Read more on the bearish case.

Edmund Ingham: Roche (RHHBY) — Ingham rates Roche Buy, arguing that its diversified pipeline spanning GLP-1/GIP, amylin, oral, anti-myostatin, and liver-focused programs could allow the company to build combinations and address a range of patient needs, providing a credible path to a large future obesity franchise. Read more on Roche's pipeline.

ALLKA Research: Novo Nordisk (NVO) — ALLKA rates Novo Nordisk Strong Buy, focusing on the company's oral GLP-1 opportunity and its Capital Markets Day pipeline sales targets as evidence that Novo's scale and metabolic expertise can support continued growth despite intensifying competition. Read more on Novo's growth strategy.

Edmund Ingham: Kailera Therapeutics (KTRA) — Ingham rates Kailera Buy, emphasizing its late-stage pipeline and cash position as the basis for an optimistic view of its potential to reach commercial scale in the oral obesity segment. Read more on the bullish Kailera case.

Terry Chrisomalis: Kailera Therapeutics (KTRA) — Chrisomalis rates Kailera Hold, arguing that available efficacy data does not yet establish meaningful differentiation from existing oral competitors, and that key clinical and regulatory catalysts remain distant enough to limit near-term conviction. Read more on the cautious Kailera view.

data.title: Biggest risk is of an inflationary mindset setting in, says Cleveland Fed's Hammack
data.description:
The biggest risk is of an inflationary mindset setting in, according to Beth Hammack, CEO of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland.

With an inflationary mindset, Hammack means businesses and households become tolerant of inflation. They will expect this inflation to continue and persist.

"We need to make sure the policy is at a restrictive stance to help bring things back down to target," she said.

Hammack was speaking on a policy panel before the Inflation: Drivers and Dynamics Conference 2026.

Developing... Check back for updates.

data.title: DOJ closes probe of CrowdStrike deals - Bloomberg
data.description:
The US Department of Justice has ended a probe into deals that CrowdStrike (CRWD) made with a distributor.

In July, DOJ lawyers told people involved in the investigation that they had finished their investigation and wouldn't bring any criminal or civil actions, according to a Bloomberg report on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter.

CrowdStrike representatives didn’t respond to calls and emails seeking comment Thursday and Friday from Bloomberg.

Bloomberg reported last May that US prosecutors were investigating a $32 million deal between CrowdStrike (CRWD) and distributor Carahsoft  Technology to supply cybersecurity to the Internal Revenue Service. 

In June of last year, CrowdStrike (CRWD) disclosed that it received requests for information from the DOJ and the US Securities and Exchange Commission related to the company's recognition of revenue and reporting of annual recurring revenue for transactions with certain customers.

data.title: Target is winning back more customers with value offerings, organized stores
data.description:
Jefferies updated investors that its recent channel checks of Target (TGT) stores indicated that customers appear highly responsive to promotional offerings across multiple categories, a positive sign for the retailer. Seasonal and category merchandise initiatives were also noted to be driving engagement.

Analyst Corey Tarlowe and his team observed strength in the apparel department at Target (TGT) stores, which appeared well-presented and well-stocked. "We also observed a clear customer response to promotional activity across several categories. Multiple items bearing promotional signage or markdown stickers appeared to have lower inventory levels than surrounding merchandise, suggesting consumers continue to engage with value-oriented offerings," wrote Tarlowe.

Looking ahead, Tarlowe continues to believe investors might not be factoring in the magnitude of Target's (TGT) merchandising transformation and the potential for it to support sustained traffic growth and margin expansion over time.

Jefferies has a Buy rating on Target (TGT) and a price target of $185.
